"""A lexical detector of statement/variable names in source code.

The strongest response is to indented names in Python-looking code. Names
following declaration words, loop introducers, and line indentation are
recognized, including adjacent pieces of the same identifier. Keywords
and most expression interiors are weaker. A small comma response follows
a recognized name. This is a heuristic, not a full syntax parser.

The inferred code style and short trailing text reset at document changes.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
OTHER, LINE_HEAD, LOOP_NAME, DECLARED_NAME = range(4)

KEYWORDS = set('''if else elif for while do return yield raise break continue try except
finally with import from as def class lambda pass assert del global nonlocal async await
public private protected static final abstract synchronized virtual override namespace
package using include switch case default throw throws new delete sizeof typedef struct
enum interface function fn func impl mod use trait match let const var mut type
end then fi done echo print printf console self this super None True False null true false
in is and or not instanceof extends implements void'''.split())
TYPES = set('''int float double bool boolean char byte short long unsigned signed
string String Object Integer Long Double Float List Map Set dict list tuple bytes
size_t auto val var const let mut dynamic real dim Dim For Integer Variant'''.split())
DECL = TYPES


def strength(role, internal_underscore, lhs_comma, python_style,
             first, indent, length, adjoining, frequency, tab,
             keyword, digit):
    if role == OTHER:
        if lhs_comma:
            if indent > 2:
                return 0.4298
            return 0.1567 if indent else 0.0198
        if internal_underscore:
            if not indent:
                return -0.0357 if length <= 2 else 0.0398
            if not adjoining:
                return 0.2783
            return -0.0115 if frequency <= 1 else 0.0912
        if python_style > 0:
            return -0.0347 if indent > 2 else -0.0143
        return 0.1007 if first else -0.0013

    if python_style > 0:
        if indent:
            if keyword:
                return 0.02
            return 0.1966 if digit else 1.2605
        if role == DECLARED_NAME:
            return -0.012
        return 0.0825 if frequency <= 2 else 0.352
    if tab:
        if keyword:
            return 0.0205
        return 0.28 if adjoining else 0.4933
    if indent > 7:
        return 0.0597 if keyword else 0.336
    return 0.1714 if first else 0.0256


@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def token_properties(text):
    name = text.strip()
    identifier = bool(re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z_0-9$]*', name))
    frequency = zipf_frequency(name.strip('_$').lower(), 'en') if identifier else 0.
    return (identifier, name in KEYWORDS, len(name), frequency,
            '_' in name, name.isdigit())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', OTHER, 0)
    _, context, active, python_style = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    # Treat escaped source listings like literal lines of source.
    text = text.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\t', '\t').replace('\\r', '\r')
    previous_line = context.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    whitespace = re.match(r'^\s*', text)[0]
    line = (context + whitespace).rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    clean = re.sub(r'^\s*[+>-]?\s*(?:\d+\t)?', '', line)
    identifier, keyword, length, frequency, internal_underscore, digit = token_properties(text)
    adjoining = bool(text and not text[0].isspace() and line
                     and re.search(r'[A-Za-z_0-9$]$', line))
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z_0-9$]*', line)
    last = words[-1] if words else ''
    role = OTHER
    if identifier or digit:
        if adjoining:
            role = active
        elif not clean:
            role = LINE_HEAD
        elif re.search(r'\bfor\s*\(?\s*$', line, re.I):
            role = LOOP_NAME
        elif last in DECL and re.search(r'[\s*&]+$', line):
            role = DECLARED_NAME
        elif (last not in {'def', 'function', 'func', 'fn'}
              and re.search(r'\b(?:public|private|protected)\s+[\w<>\[\], ]+\s+$', line)):
            role = DECLARED_NAME
        elif re.search(r'(?:^|[;{}])\s*[A-Z]\w*(?:<[^>]*>)?\s+$', line):
            role = DECLARED_NAME
    lhs_comma = text.strip() == ',' and active != OTHER
    indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(' \t'))
    first, tab = not context, '\t' in line
    value = strength(role, internal_underscore, lhs_comma, python_style,
                     first, indent, length, adjoining, frequency, tab,
                     keyword, digit)
    if identifier or digit:
        active = role
    elif ('\n' in text or text.strip()) and not lhs_comma:
        active = OTHER
    if '\n' in text:
        completed = previous_line + text.split('\n', 1)[0]
        # Infer Python from complete lines, never from future tokens.
        python_line = (r'^\s*(?:def |from .* import |import [\w.]|'
                       r'(?:if|for|while|elif|except|with)\b.*:\s*$)')
        other_line = r';\s*$|\b(?:const|let|var|function|package)\s|#include'
        if re.search(python_line, completed) and ';' not in completed:
            python_style = 1
        elif re.search(other_line, completed):
            python_style = -1
        elif (python_style == 0 and ';' not in completed
              and re.search(r'^\s*[\w_]+\s*=', completed)):
            python_style = 1
        if re.match(r'^\s*```(?:python|py)\b', completed):
            python_style = 1
        elif completed.strip() == '```':
            python_style = 0
    return (doc, (context + text)[-250:], active, python_style), float(value)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 2805: fires on variable names being written
at the start of a code statement (the left-hand side of an assignment or a loop variable).

Plain-language rule, applied token by token:
  * Look at the line so far. If it is only indentation, an optional declaration word
    (let, var, const, for, int, double, ...), and one or more plain names separated by
    commas or dots, then the current token is a name in "target position", i.e. the
    thing the statement is about to assign to.
  * Ignore keywords (if, return, print, ...). Capitalised names (types, classes) and
    dotted attribute paths (self.x) fire only weakly.
  * Strength: a small baseline; higher when the line is indented (inside a block) and
    when the recent text is assignment-heavy code (several `name = ...` lines in the
    last ~400 characters); highest when both hold.
  * Everywhere else (prose, right-hand sides, arguments, punctuation) it predicts 0.

This is a rough, concept-level description. It captures only part of the component's
variance (see the explanation): the activation is also spread over many small values
on punctuation and digits that no simple rule captures.
"""

import re

READS = ()

KEYWORDS = {"if", "else", "elif", "while", "return", "print", "def", "class", "import",
            "from", "with", "try", "except", "raise", "assert", "del", "yield", "lambda",
            "not", "and", "or", "is", "new", "function", "func", "case", "switch", "throw"}

# Declaration words that may precede the name being written.
DECL_WORDS = (r"(?:for|let|var|const|val|local|int|double|float|char|long|bool|String"
              r"|private|public|static|final)")

# The line so far: optional declaration words, then names separated by commas or dots.
TARGET = re.compile(r"\s*(?:" + DECL_WORDS + r"\*?\s+)*\$?[A-Za-z_]\w*"
                    r"(?:\s*,\s*\$?[A-Za-z_]\w*|\.[A-Za-z_]\w*|\s*,\s*)*\s*")

# An assignment statement at the start of a line: `name = ...`, `name := ...`, `name += ...`.
ASSIGN = re.compile(r"(?m)^[ \t]*[A-Za-z_][\w.]*\s*(?::=|\+=|-=|=)[^=]")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "text": "", "line": ""}
    carry["text"] = (carry["text"] + tok)[-400:]
    carry["line"] = (carry["line"] + tok).split("\n")[-1]
    line = carry["line"]

    first = re.search(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*", line)
    in_target = TARGET.fullmatch(line) is not None and first is not None
    is_name_token = re.fullmatch(r"[\s$\w,.*]+", tok) is not None
    if not (is_name_token and in_target and first.group(0) not in KEYWORDS):
        return carry, 0.0

    if tok.strip()[:1].isupper() or "." in line:
        return carry, 0.03

    indented = line[:1] in (" ", "\t")
    assignment_heavy = ASSIGN.search(carry["text"]) is not None
    value = 0.1 + 0.2 * indented + 0.3 * assignment_heavy + 0.3 * indented * assignment_heavy
    return carry, float(value)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2806: a "would like" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: this component fires on the verb of a polite wish or
preference when it comes straight after a modal "would" or "'d": "I would like",
"I'd love", "we would liked". With one adverb in between ("would still like",
"would particularly like") it fires somewhat less. The "to" right after such a verb
("would like to") fires moderately. Other uses of "like" ("I like", "looks like",
"would look like", "feel like") stay near zero, so the rule checks the modal.

A filler token "··" (a run of middle dots) gets a small constant negative value.
That value comes from a single training document made only of such dots, so it is a
guess for other text.

Values are in the component's own activation units. Everything else is predicted 0.
Known limits: the large negative spikes on rare word pieces (e.g. "gy" in "Indawgyi")
are not explained, and they carry most of the component's effect on the model's output.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

MODALS = ("would", "'d", "’d")
ADVERBS = (
    "still", "also", "therefore", "particularly", "really", "just",
    "certainly", "definitely", "always", "very",
)
WISH_VERBS = {"like": 11.0, "love": 9.0, "liked": 10.0}
FILLER = "··"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    words = [s.strip() for s in prefix.token_strings]
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = len(words) - 1

    def back(k):
        # the token k steps before the one being predicted, within the same document
        i = t - k
        return words[i] if i >= 0 and docs[i] == docs[t] else ""

    word = words[t]
    value = 0.0
    if word in WISH_VERBS:
        if back(1) in MODALS:
            value = WISH_VERBS[word]
        elif back(1) in ADVERBS and back(2) in MODALS:
            value = 0.8 * WISH_VERBS[word]
    elif word == "to" and back(1) in WISH_VERBS and (back(2) in MODALS or back(3) in MODALS):
        value = 4.5
    elif word == FILLER:
        value = -1.2
    return carry, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 2807: a "Title:" document-opener detector.

What it does
- Fires strongly (about +4.4) on the colon of a document that opens with "Title:":
  the ":" right after "Title", where "Title" is the first token of a document (it
  follows the end-of-text token, or starts a packed row).
- Elsewhere it is near zero, except for a weak negative value on the first token of a
  document that follows an end-of-text token (about -0.15 on average; it depends on
  which token opens the document, which this program does not model).

Why: the spike is a document-start marker. It is the component's only large response
in the corpus (about 37 tokens in 10 million), so it accounts for most of its strong
effect on the model.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_COLON = 4.43  # activation on the ":" of a document-initial "Title:"
DOC_OPENER = -0.15  # average on a document's first token, after end-of-text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry = (document id, index of the current token within its document)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or doc != carry[0]:
        index = 0  # first token of a row, or of a new document in the row
    else:
        index = carry[1] + 1
    carry = (doc, index)

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if index == 0:
        after_end = len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "<|endoftext|>"
        return carry, (DOC_OPENER if after_end else 0.0)
    if index == 1 and token == ":" and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "Title":
        return carry, TITLE_COLON
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2808 (layer 1, MLP down projection, direction 2808).

What it does: it is a "you / ou / yu" word-start detector. It is almost silent on
ordinary text and fires on the piece of a word that begins with the sound "yoo/ou"
in Europe and Asia words and in the words "especially" and "excellent/worry":

  * Chinese 尤 / 犹 / 猶 (yóu) and the words 尤其, 尤其是, 尤为, 犹如, which mean
    "especially" or "also": strongest (about 7-10).
  * Korean 유 (as in 유럽 Europe, 유명) and 예: strong.
  * 特别是 / 特別 / 特に ("especially"): moderate.
  * 欧 / 歐 (Europe) and 亚 / 亞 (Asia), with 欧洲 / 亚洲: moderate to strong.
  * 優 / 优 / 忧 / 憂 / 悠 (yōu: excellent, worry): moderate.

"""Approximate responses to adjective and modifier endings.

Negative responses concentrate on Chinese 的, Japanese adjective/genitive
endings, and Korean adnominal suffixes. Chinese word meanings help distinguish
an adjective's 的 from an ordinary possessive 的. English dictionary glosses
are checked for adjectival uses, separating noun/adjective homonyms.
Degree-adverb phrases and percentages strengthen Chinese responses.
Separate suffix tokens usually have larger responses than fused word endings.
A small, independent positive response covers repeated middle dots.

from functools import lru_cache
import re
import regex
import cedict
import jmdict
import wordnet

JP_SUFFIX = {
    'な': -5.3,
    'の': -0.60,
    'い': -1.11,
    'く': -0.18,
    'しい': -2.35,
    'しく': -0.98,
    'した': -0.68,
    'して': -0.26,
    'する': -0.16,
    'た': -0.26,
    'ない': -0.89,
    'に': -0.24,
}
# Korean adnominal, genitive, and adverbial suffixes.
KO_SUFFIX = {
    '적인': -3.6,
    '하게': -2.8,
    '한': -3.6,
    '운': -3.0,
    '된': -3.0,
    '른': -1.6,
    '의': -0.65,
    '히': -1.2,
    '게': -0.8,
    '은': -0.16,
    '는': 0.10,
}
DEGREE_BONUS = 1.5
DEGREE_PHRASE = regex.compile(
    r'(很|更|最|较|較|太|非常|十分)\p{Script=Han}{1,4}$'
)


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def describe(text, japanese=False):
    """Longest dictionary suffix, up to six characters.

    Return adjective flags for any/first gloss, then the same flags excluding
    translations that are also nouns, and finally the word length.
    """
    dictionary = jmdict if japanese else cedict
    for length in range(min(6, len(text)), 0, -1):
        glosses = dictionary.glosses(text[-length:])
        if not glosses:
            continue
        adjective, unambiguous = [], []
        for gloss in glosses:
            for sense in re.split(r'[;,]| and | or ', gloss):
                sense = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '', sense).strip().lower()
                sense = sense.removeprefix('to be ')
                sense = re.sub(r'^(very |highly |extremely )', '', sense)
                pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(sense)
                adjective.append('adjective' in pos)
                unambiguous.append('adjective' in pos and 'noun' not in pos)
        return (any(adjective), adjective[0], any(unambiguous),
                unambiguous[0], length)
    return False, False, False, False, 0


def chinese_value(before, separate=True, adverb=False):
    adj, first, pure, first_pure, length = describe(before)
    single = adj and length == 1
    # The coefficients below distinguish standalone and word-fused markers.
    if adverb:
        return (-0.16 - 0.38 * adj + 0.07 * first - 0.11 * pure
                - 0.62 * first_pure + 0.60 * single)
    if separate:
        value = (-0.46 - 0.48 * adj - 0.66 * first - 1.28 * pure
                 - 0.71 * first_pure + 0.75 * single)
        if DEGREE_PHRASE.search(before):
            value -= DEGREE_BONUS
    else:
        value = (-0.15 - 0.14 * adj - 0.36 * first - 0.28 * pure
                 - 0.38 * first_pure + 0.27 * single)
    if before.endswith(tuple('我你他她它您咱俺')) or before.endswith(
        ('我们', '你们', '他们', '我們', '你們', '他們', '自己')
    ):
        return 0.0
    if before and before[-1].isdigit():
        value += 0.42 if separate else -0.21
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else b''
    new = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = history.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')

                'utf-8', errors='replace')

            if stem.endswith(('%', '％')):

        value = chinese_value(before, adverb=True)

        value = JP_SUFFIX[s]

            value += 3.7
    elif regex.fullmatch(r'[\p{Script=Han}\p{Script=Hiragana}ー]+', s):
        for ending, response in (
            ('的な', -3.1),
            ('のある', -2.2),
            ('れた', -1.5),
            ('な', -0.92),
            ('い', -0.48),
            ('く', -0.20),

            if s.endswith(ending):
                value = response
                break
        if s.endswith('の') and s not in ('この', 'その', 'あの', 'どの'):
            value = -0.40
    elif regex.fullmatch(r'\s*\p{Script=Hangul}+', s):
        value = KO_SUFFIX.get(s, 0.0)
        if s not in KO_SUFFIX and s.endswith(tuple(KO_SUFFIX)):
            value = -0.3
    elif len(s) > 1 and set(s) == {'·'}:
        value = 0.86
    return (doc, (history + new)[-48:]), float(value)

    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP component 2812: the root of a fully qualified Java/Kotlin package name.

It fires on the reverse-domain root that opens a package name (`com`, `org`, `net`,
`io`, `br`, ...) when that root begins a qualified name rather than a host name:
`import com.google...`, `package org.apache...`, `at org.junit...` in a stack trace,
`public com.google.api...` as a type, or `/org/` in a `/java/org/...` source path.
The size depends on the word before the root: after `package` it is largest, then
`import`, then the `/java/` path, a stack-trace `at`, and a modifier like `static`.
A few weak responses: `.com` after `github`, and `import` at the start of a line.
Everything else (a root after a dot, as in `.apache.org`, or in prose) predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

ROOTS = {"com", "org", "net", "io", "br", "uk", "dev", "id", "sh", "ai", "cc", "ac", "edu", "gov"}

# Approximate mean activation of a root that follows each word.
LEAD_IN = {
    "package": 40.0,
    "import": 22.0,
    "/java": 22.0,
    "at": 18.0,
    "static": 16.0,
    "public": 11.0,
    "private": 11.0,
    "protected": 11.0,
    "new": 12.0,
    "implements": 12.0,
    "extends": 12.0,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = cur.strip(" \t/.")
    value = 0.0
    if len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev_raw = prefix.token_strings[-2]
        prev = prev_raw.strip(" \t")
        if word in ROOTS and not prev_raw.endswith("."):
            value = LEAD_IN.get(prev, 0.0)
            if prev == "at" and word not in ("com", "org", "net", "io"):
                value = 0.0
            if cur.startswith("/") and value == 0.0:
                value = 10.0  # a root as a path segment, e.g. .../maven2/org/...
        if cur == "/java" and prev_raw.endswith(("/main", "/test")):
            value = 10.0
        if cur == ".com" and prev_raw.endswith("ithub"):
            value = 3.5
        if cur.strip(" \t") == "import" and prev_raw.rstrip(" \t\r\n").endswith(";"):
            value = 5.0
    return carry, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 2813: the document-opening "Title:" detector.

In plain terms: this component is almost silent. Its one strong, reliable behaviour is on
the colon of a metadata label that opens a document. When a document's first token is
"Title" and the next token is ":" (as in "<|endoftext|>Title: ..."), its activation is
about -14.5, with high causal importance. The same "Title:" in the middle of a document,
or after a chat marker, is ~0.

This program predicts exactly that: -14.5 on the colon of a document-opening "Title:",
and 0 at every other position.

What it leaves out: about half of the component's variance sits on word fragments in the
middle of split words (e.g. "Ch|ung", "Gr|unde"). Those values are large in both signs,
and no word, script, or preceding-piece rule we tried predicts the sign, so they are
predicted as 0.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

OPENING_TITLE_VALUE = -14.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    value = 0.0
    if len(toks) >= 2 and toks[-1] == ":" and toks[-2].strip() == "Title":
        # "Title" must be the first token of its document (or of the row).
        opens_document = len(toks) == 2 or docs[-3] != docs[-2]
        if opens_document:
            value = OPENING_TITLE_VALUE
    return carry, value

    "одна из", "l'un des", "satu dari").

It is strongest on the link itself ("of" after "one" or "which", about 11-12). The
article after the link ("one of THE") gets about 40% of the quantifier's value. Quantifiers
that split off a total or a part ("all of", "most of", "half of", "part of") give nothing,
and a narrowed quantifier ("only one of", "each one of") gives less.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation on the link after each quantifier or number, by language.
SELECTOR = {

    "eine": 12, "einer": 12, "eines": 12, "einem": 11, "einen": 9, "ein": 7,

# Words that link a quantifier to its group: "of" and its counterparts.
LINKS = {"of", "or", "de", "des", "dei", "delle", "di", "из", "من", "der", "das", "die", "von"}

# A narrowed quantifier ("at least one of", "each one of") gives less.
MODIFIER = {"least": 0.6, "only": 0.6, "every": 0.45, "each": 0.45, "any": 0.45, "not": 0.45}

# Copulas before "among": "are among the best" fires, "particularly among" does not.
COPULAS = {"are", "were", "is", "was", "be", "been", "being"}

# Articles that follow a link: "one of THE best".
ARTICLES = {"the", "les", "los", "las", "der", "die", "das", "il", "la", "le", "el"}


def _word(s):
    # Lower-case word, with spaces and surrounding punctuation removed: ' "One' -> 'one'.
    return s.strip().lower().strip("\"'“”‘’-–—()[]*.,:;!?")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strs = prefix.token_strings
    n = len(strs)
    docs = prefix.document_ids

    def back(k):
        # The word k tokens before the current one; "" across a document break.
        if n - 1 - k < 0 or docs[n - 1 - k] != docs[-1]:
            return ""
        return _word(strs[n - 1 - k])

    cur = back(0)
    prev = back(1)
    if cur in LINKS:
        if prev == "out":  # "two out of", "7 out of"
            return carry, 5.0 if back(2).isdigit() or back(2) in SELECTOR else 0.0
        value = float(SELECTOR.get(prev, 0.0))
        if cur == "or":  # "one or more": weaker than "one of"
            value *= 0.4
        return carry, value * MODIFIER.get(back(2), 1.0)
    if cur in ("among", "amongst"):
        return carry, 9.0 if prev in COPULAS else 1.5
    if (cur in ARTICLES or cur in ("more", "both")) and prev in LINKS:
        return carry, 0.4 * float(SELECTOR.get(back(2), 0.0))
    return carry, 0.0
